question: Should Feishu/Lark plain non-topic group chats support current-conversation `thread=true` subagent binding, and what conversation identity should that binding use?
rationale: The code can be changed mechanically, but choosing whole-group, sender-scoped, topic-only, configured-route, or unsupported semantics affects session state, message delivery, compatibility, and user expectations.

options.title: Define plain-group binding semantics
options.body: Approve a concrete Feishu plain-group contract and implement it with regression tests for DM, topic, sender-topic, and plain group behavior.

options.title: Keep topic-only binding
options.body: Document that persistent subagent binding is supported only in DMs and topic conversations, and point plain groups to static group bindings or topic mode.

options.title: Defer to broader channel policy
options.body: Hold this issue until the generic channel threading policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/56307 decides how channels declare automatic thread/session behavior.

recommendation.title: Define plain-group binding semantics
recommendation.body: Approve a concrete Feishu plain-group contract and implement it with regression tests for DM, topic, sender-topic, and plain group behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the freshest core thread-binding refactor touching the permanent session-binding path and can route Feishu-specific review to plugin owners.
